name: Muhammad Ali
bio: Three-time world heavyweight boxing champion and activist, widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time.

name: George W Bush
bio: 43rd President of the United States (2001-2009), leading the country's response to the September 11 attacks.

name: Winston Churchill
bio: British Prime Minister who led the United Kingdom to victory in World War II. A Nobel laureate in Literature and one of history's great orators.

name: Hillary Clinton
bio: US Secretary of State, Senator, First Lady, and the first woman to win a major party's presidential nomination (2016).

name: Bill Clinton
bio: 42nd President of the United States (1993-2001), presiding over the longest peacetime economic expansion in American history.

name: Kurt Cobain
bio: Frontman of Nirvana, whose album 'Nevermind' defined the grunge era; died at 27.

name: Charles Darwin
bio: Naturalist whose theory of evolution by natural selection reshaped the biological sciences.

name: Princess Diana
bio: Princess of Wales and a global humanitarian icon, renowned for her charity work and immense public affection until her death in 1997.

name: Albert Einstein
bio: Theoretical physicist who developed relativity, won the 1921 Nobel Prize, and became the modern icon of genius.

name: Sigmund Freud
bio: Founder of psychoanalysis, one of the most influential and debated thinkers of the modern age.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
bio: Leader of India's non-violent independence movement against British rule. His philosophy of satyagraha (truth-force) inspired civil-rights and freedom movements across the world.

name: Prince Harry
bio: Duke of Sussex, military veteran and founder of the Invictus Games for wounded servicemembers.

name: Jimi Hendrix
bio: Widely regarded as the greatest electric guitarist in music history, despite a career of only four years; died at 27.

name: Adolf Hitler
bio: Dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945. His Nazi regime instigated the Second World War and perpetrated the Holocaust — making him one of history's most consequential and destructive figures. Included here purely as a birth-certificate-confirmed (AA) chart for study.

name: Queen Elizabeth II
bio: The longest-reigning British monarch (1952-2022), a global symbol of continuity and duty across seven decades.

name: King Charles III
bio: King of the United Kingdom since 2022, and a lifelong advocate for the environment and architecture.

name: Michael Jackson
bio: The 'King of Pop', whose album 'Thriller' remains the best-selling of all time; a revolutionary performer and dancer.

name: Angelina Jolie
bio: Academy Award-winning actress, filmmaker and humanitarian, and a UN goodwill ambassador for refugees.

name: Carl Jung
bio: Founder of analytical psychology, introducing concepts like the collective unconscious, archetypes and introversion/extraversion.

name: John F Kennedy
bio: 35th President of the United States, the youngest elected to the office. Led the nation through the Cuban Missile Crisis and launched the Apollo programme; assassinated in 1963.

name: John Lennon
bio: Co-founder of The Beatles, singer-songwriter and peace activist; one of the most influential musicians in history.

name: Madonna
bio: The 'Queen of Pop', the best-selling female recording artist of all time, famed for continual reinvention.

name: Nelson Mandela
bio: Anti-apartheid revolutionary who, after 27 years imprisoned, became South Africa's first democratically-elected President and a global symbol of reconciliation. Nobel Peace laureate.

name: Paul McCartney
bio: Co-founder of The Beatles and one of the most successful composers and performers of all time.

name: Marilyn Monroe
bio: Hollywood icon and one of the most enduring symbols of stardom, celebrated for films like 'Some Like It Hot'.

name: Jim Morrison
bio: Poet and lead singer of The Doors, an emblem of 1960s counterculture who died at 27.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
bio: India's first Prime Minister (1947-1964) and a principal architect of the modern Indian nation-state, its democracy and its foreign policy of non-alignment.

name: Barack Obama
bio: 44th President of the United States (2009-2017) and the first African-American to hold the office. A former constitutional-law professor and senator, he won the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize and passed landmark healthcare reform.

name: Elvis Presley
bio: The 'King of Rock and Roll', one of the best-selling and most culturally influential musicians of the 20th century.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
bio: Largely self-taught mathematical genius whose theorems in number theory, infinite series and continued fractions continue to influence mathematics more than a century later.

name: Ronald Reagan
bio: Hollywood actor turned 40th President of the United States (1981-1989), whose tenure is associated with the end of the Cold War.

name: Taylor Swift
bio: One of the best-selling and most awarded musicians of her generation, and a record-setting live performer.

name: Nikola Tesla
bio: Inventor and electrical engineer whose alternating-current system underpins the modern power grid.

name: Donald Trump
bio: Businessman, media personality and 45th (and 47th) President of the United States. Built a global real-estate and branding empire before entering politics and winning the 2016 election.

name: Swami Vivekananda
bio: Hindu monk and philosopher who brought Vedanta and Yoga to the West. His 1893 address at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago made him a global spiritual figure.

name: Prince William
bio: Prince of Wales and heir to the British throne, focused on conservation, mental health and homelessness.

name: Oprah Winfrey
bio: Media proprietor and talk-show host who became North America's first Black multi-billionaire and a global philanthropist.

name: Mahendra Singh Dhoni
bio: Indian cricketer and one of the most successful captains in the sport's history — the only captain to win all three major ICC white-ball trophies (2007 T20 World Cup, 2011 ODI World Cup, 2013 Champions Trophy). Celebrated wicket-keeper batsman and finisher, nicknamed 'Captain Cool'. (Birth time approximate.)

name: Virat Kohli
bio: Indian cricketer regarded as one of the greatest batsmen of the modern era and among the finest ODI batsmen of all time. Former captain of India across all formats, holder of numerous run-scoring records, celebrated for his aggression, consistency and fitness. Nicknamed 'King Kohli'.

name: Sri Aurobindo
bio: Indian philosopher, yogi and nationalist; founder of Integral Yoga and the Sri Aurobindo Ashram.

name: Rabindranath Tagore
bio: Bengali polymath and poet; first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature (1913).

name: Indira Gandhi
bio: First and only female Prime Minister of India; a dominant figure in 20th-century Indian politics.

name: Lokmanya Tilak
bio: Indian nationalist and independence activist — 'Swaraj is my birthright.'

name: Ramana Maharshi
bio: Revered Indian sage of Arunachala; teacher of self-inquiry (Atma Vichara) and non-dualism.

name: Paramahansa Yogananda
bio: Indian yogi who brought Kriya Yoga to the West; author of 'Autobiography of a Yogi.'

name: Napoleon Bonaparte
bio: French military commander and Emperor who dominated early-19th-century Europe.

name: Karl Marx
bio: German philosopher and economist whose theories (Marxism) reshaped world history.

name: Mother Teresa
bio: Catholic nun, Nobel Peace laureate and saint, renowned for her work with Kolkata's poor.

name: Che Guevara
bio: Argentine Marxist revolutionary and guerrilla leader, a central figure of the Cuban Revolution.

name: Fidel Castro
bio: Cuban revolutionary who led Cuba for nearly five decades as Prime Minister and President.

name: Audrey Hepburn
bio: British actress and humanitarian, a defining star of Hollywood's Golden Age and a style icon.

name: Grace Kelly
bio: American Academy Award-winning actress who became Princess of Monaco.

name: Charlie Chaplin
bio: English comic actor and filmmaker; one of cinema's most influential figures of the silent era.

name: Walt Disney
bio: American animation pioneer and entrepreneur who built a global entertainment empire.

name: Alfred Hitchcock
bio: English filmmaker, the 'Master of Suspense,' who transformed the thriller genre.

name: Isaac Newton
bio: English mathematician and physicist whose laws of motion and gravitation founded classical mechanics.

name: Galileo Galilei
bio: Italian astronomer and physicist, the 'father of observational astronomy' and modern science.

name: Bill Gates
bio: Co-founder of Microsoft and one of the world's foremost philanthropists.

name: Steve Jobs
bio: Co-founder of Apple who reshaped personal computing, music, phones and animation.

name: Warren Buffett
bio: American investor and philanthropist, among the most successful investors of all time.

name: Elon Musk
bio: Entrepreneur behind Tesla and SpaceX; among the wealthiest and most influential figures in tech.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
bio: Co-founder and CEO of Facebook/Meta, pioneer of the social-media era.

name: Margaret Thatcher
bio: First female Prime Minister of the UK, the 'Iron Lady' who reshaped British politics.

name: Angela Merkel
bio: First female Chancellor of Germany and a leading figure in European politics for 16 years.

name: Pope Francis
bio: Argentine-born head of the Catholic Church; the first Jesuit and first Latin American pope.

name: Vladimir Putin
bio: Long-serving President of Russia and a dominant figure in 21st-century geopolitics.

name: Dalai Lama XIV
bio: Tenzin Gyatso, spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism and Nobel Peace laureate.

name: Tony Blair
bio: Prime Minister of the UK (1997-2007), leader of 'New Labour.'

name: Freddie Mercury
bio: British singer and frontman of Queen, one of rock's greatest vocalists and showmen.

name: David Bowie
bio: English singer-songwriter and actor, a pioneering, ever-reinventing icon of rock.

name: Bob Dylan
bio: American singer-songwriter and Nobel laureate; a defining voice of the 1960s.

name: Mick Jagger
bio: English singer and frontman of The Rolling Stones.

name: Prince
bio: American singer, multi-instrumentalist and producer of boundless musical range.

name: Tiger Woods
bio: American golfer, one of the greatest and most successful in the sport's history.

name: Pele
bio: Brazilian footballer regarded as one of the greatest of all time; three-time World Cup winner.

name: Usain Bolt
bio: Jamaican sprinter, eight-time Olympic gold medallist and the fastest man in recorded history.

name: Michael Jordan
bio: American basketball legend, six-time NBA champion, often called the greatest of all time.

name: Serena Williams
bio: American tennis champion with 23 Grand Slam singles titles, among the greatest athletes ever.

name: Ayrton Senna
bio: Brazilian Formula One driver and three-time World Champion, one of the sport's greatest.
